title: Hierarchy of hidden nonlocality: A genuine activation of Incompletability
authors: Soumajit Das, Shampa Mondal, Preeti Parashar, Atanu Bhunia
abstract: Quantum nonlocality admits several operational manifestations, one of which emerges from sets of orthogonal quantum states that cannot be perfectly distinguished by local operations and classical communication (LOCC). Such sets are regarded as nonlocal because their perfect discrimination requires global measurements. In contrast, sets that are perfectly distinguishable by LOCC are generally considered locally accessible and operationally classical. In this work, we investigate the role of incompletability in local state discrimination and introduce the notion of \emph{activation of incompletability}. Specifically, we demonstrate the existence of orthogonal sets that are initially perfectly distinguishable by LOCC and free from local redundancy, but which can be transformed via LOCC into strictly incompletable sets. We prove that activation of incompletability necessarily implies activation of nonlocality, whereas the converse fails in general, thereby establishing a hierarchy between the two activation phenomena. Furthermore, within the framework of local incoherent operations and classical communication (LICC), we show that any set whose incompletability can be activated can nevertheless be extended to a complete orthonormal basis of the Hilbert space, although the resulting completed basis is no longer perfectly distinguishable by LOCC. Our results uncover a fundamental interplay among local distinguishability, incompletability, coherence, and nonlocality, and provide new insight into the structure of locally accessible quantum information.
summary: This work develops a rigorous framework to compare different forms of quantum correlation by introducing the concept of 'activation of incompletability.' The authors prove that this phenomenon implies nonlocality, establishing a strict hierarchy between the two. This sheds new light on how local distinguishability breaks down when considering fundamental structural properties like basis completion.
main_problem: The paper investigates the operational relationship between local distinguishability, quantum incompletability, and nonlocality for sets of orthogonal quantum states.
main_result: It establishes a strict hierarchy: activating incompletability implies activating nonlocality, but the reverse implication fails. Furthermore, it shows that such activation can be achieved while extending the set to a basis that is no longer perfectly distinguishable by LOCC.
method: The analysis uses theoretical constructions involving Local Operations and Classical Communication (LOCC) protocols applied to multipartite quantum states, defining concepts like 'activation of incompletability' via measurements.
model_or_system: The system under study consists of sets of mutually orthogonal quantum states in tensor product Hilbert spaces ($\mathcal{H}_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes \mathcal{H}_n$), analyzed using the operational constraints of LOCC and LICC.
key_observables: Local distinguishability (by LOCC), Incompletability, Nonlocality, Quantum Coherence, and local redundancy.
important_parameters: The dimensionality of the Hilbert space ($d_1, d_2, \dots$) and the specific structure of the orthogonal state sets are crucial parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis is fundamentally restricted to operations achievable via LOCC or LICC, which defines the operational boundaries for distinguishability claims.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate the hierarchy between activation phenomena (Incompleteness $\implies$ Nonlocality) and show examples of states that activate nonlocality without activating incompletability.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by defining necessary concepts (OPLM, locally irreducible/indistinguishable sets), then constructing explicit counterexamples ($S_3$) to establish the hierarchy, and finally analyzing the implications within the LICC framework concerning coherence.
why_interesting: It provides a deep resource-theoretic understanding of quantum correlations, linking geometric properties (completeness) to operational limitations (LOCC distinguishability) in a way that is highly relevant for characterizing genuine nonclassicality.
